question: The EU anti-racism strategy 2026–2030 is built on the death of George Floyd and the Black Lives Matter movement. That origin matters, as it imports an American racial narrative into EU policy: racism flows in one direction only, with minorities as victims and white citizens as perpetrators. That double standard is written into the strategy itself.

It names anti-Black racism, antigypsyism, antisemitism, anti-Asian racism and anti-Muslim hatred. White Europeans as potential victims: absent. By design. This asymmetry is not theoretical. It is deadly. The Henry Nowak case shows where this logic ends: a white student fatally stabbed, then handcuffed after his attacker falsely invoked racism. The accusation overruled reality.
A doctrine designed to fight discrimination produced the opposite: unequal credibility before the law, at the cost of a life. 1.
What empirical evidence demonstrates that EU-supported anti-racism training does not create credibility presumptions based on skin colour?
Will the Commission include safeguards against weaponised racism accusations in its upcoming policing compendium?
Will the Commission revise the EU anti-racism strategy 2026–2030 to guarantee equal protection for all citizens regardless of skin colour?
